mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved in three of the last four weeks (-38.1 to -29.1), and each step of transit recovery returns discretionary trips to retail-recreation venues, so transit momentum alone carries RETAIL_REC above its trailing 28-day mean of -28.5 over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -38.1 at t-3w to -29.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is at or below -28.5 even while TRANSIT continues to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen from +9.4 to +6.6, so a weekly RESIDENTIAL mean below +7 marks households converting stay-at-home time into out-of-home trips; below that threshold RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean drops below +7.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from +9.4 at t-3w to +6.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: Weeks with RESIDENTIAL below +7.0 are followed by a two-week RETAIL_REC mean at or below the trailing 28-day mean at least as often as weeks above it.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of TRANSIT (-38.1 to -29.1) and WORKPLACES (-19.6 to -16.6) rebuilds the weekday commute-and-errand loop; only when both rise together does retail-recreation footfall follow, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -23.4 at t-2w to -16.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together for two consecutive weeks, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean fails to exceed the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active reopening regime with capacity caps being lifted, venue capacity limits are the binding constraint on retail-recreation visits; each relaxation step adds to RETAIL_REC and pushes the next four weeks above the trailing mean of -28.5.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -35.7 at t-3w to -23.4 at t-0w during the reopening window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls below its trailing 28-day mean in the weeks immediately following capacity-cap relaxations.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS spiked to +39.7 at t-1w while RETAIL_REC stayed near -23, showing warm-weather recreation demand diverting into free outdoor venues; a PARKS weekly mean above +30 predicts lower RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean above +30 percent for one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached +39.7 at t-1w while RETAIL_REC was -22.0
failure_condition: Weeks with PARKS above +30 are followed by a two-week RETAIL_REC mean at or above the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM holds near zero (mean +0.9) while RETAIL_REC sits at -28.5; that 25-point gap is discretionary avoidance, and as the gap narrows RETAIL_REC mean-reverts upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC minus GROCERY_PHARM gap narrows by 5 points from its t-0w value of -25.3
failure_condition: The RETAIL_REC-minus-GROCERY_PHARM gap widens further and the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean stays below -28.5.

mechanism_narrative: A transit stall or reversal (t-0w -29.1 versus t-1w -28.4) marks renewed caution under a variant or re-tightening regime; retail-recreation trips are cut first, driving RETAIL_REC below -28.5 within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean declines by more than 3 points week-on-week

failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT declines more than 3 points week-on-week, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds -28.5.

mechanism_narrative: The single-week RETAIL_REC dip from -22.0 to -23.4 is weather-driven noise, since PARKS simultaneously fell from +39.7 to +16.6; as outdoor conditions normalize, RETAIL_REC recovers within one week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls week-on-week while PARKS falls at least 15 points in the same week
